rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deleted verb saved is understood from context; its omission signals that Thamud’s punishment was less severe than ʿĀd’s.
rows.anchor: وحذف ( نجينا ) هنا يدل على أن عذابهم دون عذاب عاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khizy is a disgrace whose shame becomes visible and of the sort one feels ashamed to experience.
rows.anchor: والخزي : العيب الذي تظهر فضيحته ويستحي من مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is strong because He overcomes everything, and mighty because He can prevent others without being overcome or resisted.
rows.anchor: فهو يغلب كل شيء { العزيز * } اي القادر على منع غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blast is grammatically treated without the feminine marker, which Biqaʿi says signals its immense force.
rows.anchor: وأشار إلى عظمة هذه الصيحة بإسقاط علامة التأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He first explains them as fallen face down; he also reports the alternative that they crouched dead and motionless on their knees.
rows.anchor: أي ساقطين على وجوههم , وقيل : جاثين على الركب موتى لا حراك بهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative gloss takes juthūm as sitting on the knees, dead and motionless.
rows.anchor: وقيل : جاثين على الركب موتى لا حراك بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi recalls his earlier contrast in al-Aʿrāf between plural dwellings with the blast here and singular dwelling with the earthquake there.
rows.anchor: وتقدم سر التعبير بالديار مع الصيحة والدار مع الرجفة في الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Juthūm is a euphemism for death; saying they became so by morning heightens the terror and regret of their sudden stillness as though they had never existed.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الجثوم كناية عن الموت أوضحه بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase depicts them as having vanished without a trace; ghana can suggest living in prosperity and song, while al-maghānī means dwellings and the root sense is sufficiency.
rows.anchor: والمغاني : المنازل , وأصل الغناء الاكتفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning normally brings waking, rest, and capacity for desired activity, so their becoming utterly still by morning intensifies warning and lament.
rows.anchor: وقال { أصبحوا } زيادة في التخويف والتأسيف بما وقع لهم ن التحسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alā is an alerting formula used for momentous matters, meant to keep a heedless listener from overlooking what follows.
rows.anchor: مفتتحا بالأداة التي لا تقال إلا عندالأمور الهائلة

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani analyzes alā as the interrogative alif entering lā: together they produce an alerting sense through affirmation and negation.
rows.anchor: قال الرماني : وهي ألف الاستفهام دخلت على ( لا ) فالألف تقتضي معنى , و ( لا ) تنفي معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi explains lā as negating what follows and the interrogative denial as negating lā; the double negation affirms the point especially emphatically.
rows.anchor: أن ( لا ) دخلت على ما بعدها فنفته , ثم دخلت عليها همزة الإنكار فنفتها , ومن المعلوم أن نفي النفي إثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declinable reading of Thamud signals contempt for their rash disobedience.
rows.anchor: قراءة الصرف دالة علىالاستخفاف بهم لطيشهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They covered over their Lord, their benefactor through creation, provision, and sending, as well as His attributes and acts.
rows.anchor: أوقعوا التغطية والستر على المحسن غليهم بالخلق والرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making kafarū transitive directly to their Lord, unlike many parallels, marks the coarseness of their unbelief.
rows.anchor: فإيصال الفعل دون قصره كما في أكثر أضرابه بيان لغلظة كفرهم

rows.speaker: غير الكسائي
rows.claim: Readers other than al-Kisaʾi leave Thamud indeclinable here, signaling their lasting banishment and distance.
rows.anchor: ترك صرفهم في قراءة غير الكسائي إيذانا بدوام لبثهم في الطرد والبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating alā confirms the condemnation and announces the permanence of their destruction.
rows.anchor: ثم كرر ذلك تأكيدا له وإعلاما بتأبيد هلاكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud may be declined when it names the tribe’s father and left indeclinable when it names the tribe; declension in the accusative was chosen for lightness.
rows.anchor: لما جاز الصرف في ثمود باعتبار أنه اسم أبي القبيلة وعدمه باعتبار إطلاقه على القبيلة اختير الصرف في النصب فقط لخفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the story of Lot, marked by his obedience without desire or fear and the danger surrounding the angels’ descent, Biqaʿi turns to the nearest famous story in time.
rows.anchor: أتبعت أقرب القصص الشهيرة إليها في الزمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midian is a tribe named for its forefather Midian, son of Abraham; Shuʿayb is called their brother.
rows.anchor: وهم قبيلة أبيهم مدين بن إبراهيم عليه السلام

words: اعْبُدُوا۟ اللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb begins, like the other prophets, with the foundation of religion: worship God alone and associate nothing with Him.
rows.anchor: ما قال إخوانه من الأنبياء في البداءة بأصل الدين

words: اعْبُدُوا۟ اللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets’ agreement on one God despite distant times and lands proves their truth, since they did not learn these teachings from one another or worldly reports.
rows.anchor: واتحدت إلى الله وحده دعوتهم

rows.speaker: عمر بن محمد السهروردي
rows.claim: Al-Suhrawardi says the prophets share one source and fundamentals while their revealed laws differ according to divine wisdom and the needs of each community and age.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام شهاب الدين عمر بن محمد السهروردي في كتابه ( رشف النصائح الإيمانية

rows.speaker: عمر بن محمد السهروردي
rows.claim: Al-Suhrawardi criticizes philosophers for remaining within the visible realm and exposing ignorance and contradiction when they speculate about divinity; he invokes 59:14.
rows.anchor: إن الفلاسفة لما لم يغترفوا من بحار الأنبياء وقفت بهم أفراس أفكارهم في عالم الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After calling for justice toward God, Shuʿayb calls for justice toward His servants by forbidding their customary fraud in measures and weights, including their instruments.
rows.anchor: دعاهم إلى العدل فيما بينهم وبين عبيده في أقبح ما كانوا قد اتخذوه بعد الشرك ديدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Measure and its instrument concern quantity, while weighing and its instrument concern weight or quality.
rows.anchor: فالكيل للعدل في الكمية والوزن للعدل في الكيفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition covers every kind of reduction, whether in what is measured or in the measuring instrument itself.
rows.anchor: لا الكيل ولا آلته ولا الوزن ولا آلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their ample means should make fraud unnecessary; the reminder both encourages gratitude and warns that gratitude brings blessing.
rows.anchor: أي بسعة تغنيكم عن البخس - مرهبا ومرغبا بالإشارة للنقمة كما أن الشكر موجب للنعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The encompassing day threatens them for both fraud and associating partners, reaching young and old and all their property; it means a destructive punishment.
rows.anchor: بكم صغارا وكبارا وبأموالهم طيبا وخبيثا , أي مهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because merely avoiding reductions could mean only approximating the measure, Shuʿayb explicitly commands full delivery and, when needed, a surplus to ensure it.
rows.anchor: ولماكن عدم النقص قد يفهم منه التقريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An explicit command to do the opposite after forbidding reduction is more emphatic; repetition stresses the order’s broad benefit and blessing.
rows.anchor: ولأن التصريح بالأمر بالشيء بعد النهي عن ضده أوكد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb appeals to their kinship and strength, reminding them they should rise above low conduct and heed his concern for them.
rows.anchor: مستعطفا لهمبالتذكير بأنه منهم يسوءه ما يسءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awfū means to complete the delivery fully and well.
rows.anchor: أي أتموا إتماما حسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command covers the measured and weighed goods as well as the measuring and weighing instruments.
rows.anchor: أي , المكيل والموزون وآلتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qist means even, upright justice.
rows.anchor: أي العدل السوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated commands remove any suggestion that the measure is figurative and emphasize the order’s universal benefit and blessing.
rows.anchor: فصار الوفاء مأمورا له في هاتين الجملتين مرارا تأكيدا له وحرصا عليه لعموم نفعه وشمول بركته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi says an object may figuratively mean what it nearly reaches, discussed earlier in al-Anʿam and again at 11:104.
rows.anchor: وقد مضى في الأنعام ويأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition generalizes to every reduction in people’s property, not only measures and weights.
rows.anchor: ثم أكده أيضا بتعميم النهي عن كل نقص بذلك وغيره في جميع الأموال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bakhs is reduction in a manner of denial or humiliation; it is narrower than injustice, which means putting something in the wrong place.
rows.anchor: أي تنقصوا على وجه الجحد والإهانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb forbids acting and agitating without insight or reflection; impulsive action grows from folly into corruption, so people should consider before acting.
rows.anchor: أي تتصرفوا وتضطربوا فيها عن غير بصسرة ولا تأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi derives ʿathā from a field of acting without insight, linking it to smooth deceptive ground, a blind person searching, and the fool; he says this leads to following desire and corruption.
rows.anchor: دائرة على الطلب عن غير بصيرة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority gloss the phrase as do not deliberately commit corruption in the land.
rows.anchor: ما قا لالجمهور : ولا تفعلوا الفساد عمدا

rows.speaker: الزبيدي
rows.claim: Al-Zabidi’s Mukhtasar al-ʿAyn glosses ʿathā as equivalent to ʿātha: to hasten in corruption.
rows.anchor: وفي مختصر العين للزبيدي : عثى في الأرض بمعنى عاث يعيث عيثا , وهو الإسراع في الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi favors the idea that proceeding without reflection is inherently aligned with desire and corruption; he clarifies that hastening itself is not separately prohibited as a delay requirement.
rows.anchor: بل هو إشارة غلى أنه لا يكون الإقدام بلا تأمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wafāʾ is fulfillment of a right; bakhs is reduction and therefore more specific than injustice.
rows.anchor: والوفاء : تمام الحق ؛ والبخس : النقص , فهو أخص من الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the day encompassing is more terrifying because the day contains the punishment and the punishment in turn surrounds its victims on every side.
rows.anchor: وهو الدائر بالشيء من كل جانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image derives from an enemy’s encirclement; Biqaʿi links the same wording to the destruction of the garden in 18:42.
rows.anchor: الكهف : 42 ] وأصله من إحاطة العدو

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Majah reports Ibn ʿUmar saying that cheating in measure brings years of hardship and unjust rulers, while withholding zakat brings withheld rain; without animals, no rain would fall. No grading is stated.
rows.anchor: رواه ابن ماجة عن ابن عمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God leaves through just dealing is better than their imagined gains from fraud: blessing in their wealth and circumstances, and His continued favor and pardon.
rows.anchor: أي فضل الملك الأعلى المستجمع لصفات الكمال , وبركته في أموالكم وجميع أحوالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baqiyyah is what remains from something past and may also mean sparing or preserving someone by forgiving a fault.
rows.anchor: من أبقى عليه يبقي إبقاء

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzaz records the idiom أراك تبقي هذا ببصرك for looking at something with care, illustrating the sense of preserving or sparing.
rows.anchor: قاله الإمام أبو عبد الله القزاز في ديوانه الجامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remnant’s true benefit depends on firm faith; without faith it is only temporary worldly good, soon lost through death or departure.
rows.anchor: فهي غير مجدية إلا في الدنيا , فهي عدم لسرعة الزوال والنزوح عنها والارتحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional wording implies an appeal to believe and act on Shuʿayb’s instruction in order to attain that good.
rows.anchor: فآمنوا فاعلين ما أمرتكم به لتظفروا بالخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb is a warner, not a guardian who knows every deed and circumstance or can restrain them from corruption.
rows.anchor: أعلم جميع أعمالكم وأحوالكم وأقدر على كفكم عما يكون منها فسادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call Shuʿayb by name rather than kinship, with rudeness and harshness, and mock the influence of his prayer.
rows.anchor: سموه باسمه جفاء وغلظة وأنكروا عليه مستهزئين بصلاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They sarcastically portray his prayer as a constant commander telling them to abandon their fathers’ worship and stop doing whatever they want with their wealth.
rows.anchor: تفعل معك فعل من كان يأمر دائما بتكليفنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They describe fraud, ruined transactions, gambling, and similar practices as doing with money whatever they please, and suppose restraint would squander wealth.
rows.anchor: من قطع الدهم والدينار وإفساد المعاملة والمقامرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi traces the forms of ṣalā to connection: prayer joins servant and Lord, while supplication, seeking pardon, and Jewish synagogues also express connection; he promises a fuller account at 13:15.
rows.anchor: ومادة صلا - واوية ويائية مهموزة وغير مهموزة بجميع تقاليبها - تدور على الوصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people use ḥalīm and rashīd sarcastically, twisting the virtues into alleged patience with what relatives dislike and foolishness about money.
rows.anchor: يريدون بهذا كما زعموا - سلخه من كل ما هو متصف به دونهم من هاتين الصفتين الفائقتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their taunt is meant to accuse Shuʿayb of folly and error by mockery.
rows.anchor: وعنوا بذلك نسبته إلى السفه والغي على طريق التهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their appeal to their fathers rests on blind imitation and the presumption that ancestral practice cannot be wrong.
rows.anchor: فدارت شبهتهم في الأمرين على تلقيد الآباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb appeals to their kinship and asks them to think fairly through a hypothetical case to encourage agreement and impartiality.
rows.anchor: مستعطفا لهم بما بينهم من عواطف القرابة منبها لهم على حسن النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arāʾaytum means tell me.
rows.anchor: أي أخبروني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayyinah means proof, and the hypothetical wording presents Shuʿayb as firmly established upon proof from his Lord.
rows.anchor: أي برهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb says God granted him abundant, lawful wealth in which he wronged no one.
rows.anchor: جليلا ومالا جما حلالا لم أظلم فيه أحد

words: عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّى وَرَزَقَنِى مِنْهُ رِزْقًا حَسَنًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer to the hypothetical is omitted so the audience can consider every implication, including whether justice makes Shuʿayb foolish or allows him to abandon God's call.
rows.anchor: والجواب مجذوف لتذهب النفس فيه كل مذهب

words: وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُخَالِفَكُمْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنْهَىٰكُمْ عَنْهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb denies ever doing what he forbids, and says that leaving their fraud is guidance rather than wasteful opposition.
rows.anchor: ما فعلت قط ما نهيتكم عنه فيما مضى

words: أَنْ أُخَالِفَكُمْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنْهَىٰكُمْ عَنْهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi illustrates the point with a maxim against forbidding a vice while committing it oneself.
rows.anchor: لا تنه عن خلق وتأتي بمثله عار عليك إذا فعلت عظيم

words: إِنْ أُرِيدُ إِلَّا الْإِصْلَٰحَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb’s sole aim is reform to the limit of his capacity; his just financial conduct demonstrates that fairness is not wasteful.
rows.anchor: أي ما { أريد } أي شيئا من الأشياء { إلا الإصلاح }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His reasoning honors three rights in all conduct: God’s first, the self’s second, and other people’s third, with sincerity in each.
rows.anchor: أن العقل يجب أن يراعي في كل ما يأتي ويذر أحد حقوق ثلاثه أهمها وأعلاها حق الله وثانيها حق النفس وثالثها حق العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawfīq is the creation of a capacity that fits an act of obedience, from the idea of matching or agreement.
rows.anchor: والوفيق : خلق قدرة ما هو وفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb attributes success in reform to God alone and disclaims independent power or strength.
rows.anchor: ثم تبرأ من الحول والقوة , وأسند الأمر إلى من هو له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reliance on God entrusts affairs to Him, accepts His management, and remains committed to obedience.
rows.anchor: تفويض الأمر إليه على الرضاء بتدبيره مع التمسك بطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb turns wholly to God, renewing repentance because of the magnitude of the task; the wording also warns of resurrection and strengthens belief in return after death.
rows.anchor: يجدد التوبة لعظم الأمرن وعبر عن ذلك بعبارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After mentioning signs of divine perfection and that most believers still associate partners, Biqaʿi explains their error by God's lack of any equal; he recalls 12:105–106.
rows.anchor: شرع يبين ضلالهم في اشتراكهم المشار إليه في قوله : { وما يؤمن أكثرهم بالله إلا وهم مشركون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God has the true invocation: if called, He hears and answers as He wills; alternatively, His command clarifies truth, or His decree makes the called submit.
rows.anchor: إن دعاه أحد سمعه فأجابه - إن شاء - بما يشاء , وإن دعا هو أحدا دعوة أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who call on others beside God are the unbelievers, and the objects they invoke cannot answer them at all.
rows.anchor: أي يدعو الكافرون , وبين سفول رتبتهم بقوله : { من دونه } أي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istijābah means following a caller in the request in a way that accords with the caller’s will.
rows.anchor: والاستجابة : متابعة الداعي فيما دعا إليه بموافقة إرادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their futile invocation resembles someone stretching both hands toward water that cannot sense a call or reach his mouth; idols are just as unresponsive.
rows.anchor: كما أن الماء جماد لا يحس بدعوة هذا فلا يجيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaff is the gripping part of the hand, named from gathering its fingertips; the preposition ilā indicates that his hands do not actually reach the water.
rows.anchor: تثنية كف , وهو موضع القبض باليد , وأصله من كفه - إذا جمع أطرافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water will not reach the man’s mouth, just as the false gods do not respond to those invoking them.
rows.anchor: دون أن يصل كفاه إلى الماء - بما يدل عليه التعدية ب ( إلى )

words: وَمَا دُعَاءُ الْكَافِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse generalizes from their particular invocation by naming unbelievers as a class whose calls are always futile; idols neither harm nor benefit, and God does not answer those who neglect monotheism.
rows.anchor: مظهرا تعميما وتعليقا للحكم بالوصف

words: وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَن فِى السَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَالْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing God’s clear call by command in His books, Biqaʿi explains the call by decree through the submission of all creation, recalling 11:119.
rows.anchor: دعوة الأمرواضحة السبل جلية المناهج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sujūd means submission, compliance, and humility, as in the discussion of differing people and divine mercy at 11:119.
rows.anchor: أي يخضع وينقاد ويتذلل كما بين عند قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in heaven and earth submits to God's operative judgments and decrees.
rows.anchor: لجميع أحكامه النافذة وأقضيته الجارية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Voluntary submission is compliance with a command that the self is invited to obey.
rows.anchor: والطوع : الانقياد للأمر الذي يدعى إليه من قبل النفس

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says even an unbeliever counts as prostrating in effect, though unwilling, because need compels submission.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي رحمه الله : والكافر في حكم الساجد وإن أباه لما به من الحاجة الداعية إلى الخضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every kind of being, animate or inanimate, rational or not, spiritual or not, is humbled and governed by the Creator and Lord of command.
rows.anchor: سجود كل صنف هو تذلله وتسخره وانقياده

rows.speaker: الشيخ محيي الدين النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi says sujūd originally means humility and submission; every inanimate thing’s Quranic prostration is obedience to what it was made subject to, while placing the forehead down is the utmost form.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ محيي الدين النووي رضي الله عنه فس شرح المهذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shadows also submit because no one can change their spreading, shortening as the sun rises and lengthening as it declines.
rows.anchor: تسجد له بامتدادها على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuduww is the plural of ghadāh, the early morning or first part of the day.
rows.anchor: جمع غداة , وهي البكرة : أول النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āṣāl is the plural of aṣīl, generally the afternoon and in some places around midday; aṣīl is from mid-afternoon to sunset, the beginning from which night develops.
rows.anchor: جمع أصيل , دائما في جميع البلاد , وفي وسط النهار في بعض البلاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ẓill is the shade screening an object, while fayʾ is shade returning after the light has passed.
rows.anchor: والظل : ستر الشخص ما بإزائه , والفيء : الذي يرجع بعد ذهاب ضوئه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqaʿi traces ṣalā and its rearrangements to connection: prayer joins servant to Lord through supplication, pardon, mercy, divine praise, or formal prayer; the excerpt then begins further bodily and horse-related senses.
rows.anchor: ومادة ( صلا ) - واوية ويائية مهموزة وغير مهموزة بتراكيبها الأحد عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other derivatives of ṣalā include the middle of the back or hindquarters and a pregnant camel’s loosened hindquarter; a musallī horse is the runner immediately behind the leader.
rows.anchor: والصلا : وسط الظهر منا , أو من كل ذي أربع
